title: Service contracts document
description: Architecture-tier registry (doc 11 §6) freezing the project's service contracts. Each contract's definition lives in code (proto/Go); this document carries the frozen reference plus rationale so contracts become checkable join keys (CTR-NNNN) for downstream work packages and specifications (T4). Canonical form: registry YAML projected to {meta, data}.

type.description: Document type discriminator; fixed to `service-contracts` so the validator selects this schema.

contracts.description: The project's service contracts. At least one; each is an independently citable architecture item (CTR-NNNN) that downstream WPs realize and SPECs cite (doc 11 §7 T4).

id.description: Stable contract identifier in the form CTR-NNNN (doc 11 §3). Unique within this document and the join key downstream items use to realize this contract.

name.description: Human-readable contract name, e.g. `BillingService` or `OrderPlaced event`. Short, stable, and distinct from the code symbol if they differ.

kind.description: Contract shape: `connect-service` (a Connect/proto RPC service), `library-interface` (an in-process Go interface boundary), or `event` (an asynchronous message contract).

definition_reference.description: Frozen `path://` reference to where the definition lives in code (proto or Go) — the source of truth for the contract's shape. The document does not duplicate the definition; it points at it, e.g. `path://proto/billing/v1/billing.proto#BillingService` or `path://internal/orders/store.go#Store`.

summary.description: Markdown rationale: what this contract is for, the boundary it draws, and why it exists. Capture the negotiation context a frozen contract carries (doc 11 §6), not a restatement of the code signature.

status.description: Contract lifecycle: `draft` while negotiable; `frozen` once agreed at contract freeze. Editing a frozen contract requires a new negotiation gate (doc 11 §7 T7).

links.description: Typed upstream edges for this contract (doc 11 §3). Use `realizes` to cite the tier-P/A items it serves (≥1, doc 11 §7 T3); `refines` for same-tier elaboration. Direction is upstream only; reverse edges are derived.
